page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Split the modulus using its definition
steps.margin_note: First mark. |2−x| changes sign at x=2 — the midpoint of the given interval [0,4].
steps.memory_tip: The split point for |a−x| is always x=a — here a=2.
steps.why: |2−x| changes sign at x=2, where 2−x=0, so the integral over 0 to 4 must be split into the piece before x=2 and the piece after it.
common_mistakes: Splitting at x=0 or x=4 instead of the correct point x=2.
Using the wrong sign on one of the two pieces.

steps.label: Integrate each piece and add
steps.margin_note: Second mark. The two pieces contribute 2 each by the symmetry of the V-shape about x=2.
steps.memory_tip: Since 2 is exactly the midpoint of [0,4], the two triangular areas either side of x=2 are equal.
steps.why: Evaluating each bracket at its limits and adding the two results gives the total area of the V-shape formed by |2−x| between x=0 and x=4.
common_mistakes: An arithmetic slip in (8−8)−(2−4), e.g. reading it as 0−(−2)=−2 instead of +2.
Forgetting to add the two separate integrals together.
